placement.position_note: PARTY-LINE FRONTAGE, DERIVED FROM THE COMMITTED PLAT (T-0078). This building does not stand centred on a lot at a typology setback: it stands ON the north face of blk_lake_franklin, the block's Lake Street frontage, whose line and bearing are read from the block boundary in data/traces/vectors/thompson_lots.json — the same committed geometry the lot grid and the corridor gate are derived from. Its front wall is 1.50 m back from that lot line, which is the closest line the plat module's own margin allows and is not a measurement of this frontage, and its east wall is fixed by the west wall of recon_1835_blk_lake_franklin_c2_01, which it shares a party line with. The bearing is the face's own, so the front looks square at Lake Street. The run carries no lateral offset, because a shared party wall is one wall and cannot wander. WHAT IS INVENTED IS STILL EVERYTHING THAT MATTERS: that a building stood here at all, which building it was, and that these particular units stood shoulder to shoulder. What the 1834 South Water Street view supports is the TREATMENT — a continuous working row of party walls rather than detached cottages set back on grass. The treatment is what this placement takes from it, and a run standing on any other face of the town is borrowing it from that one street: the view draws a row, it does not place this row. Standing on a derived block face is not standing on a recovered lot, and the side lot lines this row crosses were always conjectural.
placement.symbolic_location: Anonymous reconstructed roof in the South Division block bounded by Lake, Wells, Randolph and Franklin; standing ON the Lake Street frontage itself, one unit of the party-line row along it

residents.basis: HOUSED HERE BY THE DEAL, NOT RECORDED HERE (L354). The sources stop short of 1 July 1835 for this household and nothing puts it anywhere else; the town's rule (T-1386) counts it present, and no source says where it slept. The roof is the invention and the people are not.

persons.name: Alexis Thomas Blanchemontagne
persons.note: THE ST CYR REGISTER OF 1833-1835 NAMES THIS PERSON IN THE PARISH. Read from church_1833_1835. THE GRADE IS THE OWNER'S RATIFIED LADDER OF 2026-09-03 (G2c), applied to every identity at once by tools/consolidate_resident_evidence.py and spent onto this card by tools/mint_civic_residents.py; the evidence blocks below carry the reading AS READ, its locator and the record it came from, so the page can be gone back to. WHAT IS RECONSTRUCTED: everything except the person and the sources — no dwelling, no trade, no origin, no family, no party. A BOUND FROM THE RECORD, NOT AN ARRIVAL. church_1833_1835 names this person at Chicago by 4 October 1835 and nothing says when they came. THE BOUND FALLS AFTER THE SCENE DATE and the record says so rather than narrowing it: the earliest source that names this person is later than 1 July 1835, so they may have arrived after the day this scene models. present_on_scene_date is `uncertain` for that reason. No figure is drawn (L1).

frontage.why: T-0028, the block programme's own ticket, and the first block it has opened since 2026-08-23 — the run that day found no block left to open and filed the street control (T-0163) that was blocking them. This one needed no new control: it has stood `open` in the schedule with two free lots throughout, and what changed is the DEAL. Until T-0213 weighted the trade families onto the business front on 2026-08-26 this block was dealt I3, which tools/generate_block_infill.py refuses by name, alongside F3; T-0188 read that pair on 2026-08-27 and recorded that the block 'cannot carry a three-unit run as dealt'. Re-derived today with tools/reconcile_665.py the deal is A1, D1, D5 and F3, so three of the four are buildable and the block opens. THE FACE IS MEASURED RATHER THAN ASSUMED, by the command T-A14 made of it — tools/measure_street_frontage.py lake randolph franklin wells — and on the committed dataset Lake carries 16 documented records and 8 inferred households within 25 m of its centreline against Randolph's 7 and 7. The reconstruction column is this programme's own output and does not vote. Lake is this block's business face by the town's own record, so the free Lake lot takes the row and the free Randolph lot is left open. THE END RULE IS T-A11'S, READ ON THIS BLOCK: the Dearborn Street drawbridge — the only crossing of the main stem in July 1835 — stands EAST of this block, so the town-centre end of the frontage is the east one, and the run is anchored there and graded that way: the deep-plan frame cottage at the east end and the older log dwelling west of it. NO COORDINATE IS AUTHORED: the line, its bearing, the lot's own stretch of it and the end the run packs away from are all read from the committed block boundary in data/traces/vectors/thompson_lots.json, and the 1.5 m setback is the plat module's own lot margin rather than a measurement of this frontage. This face carried no frontage record before this run — tools/measure_street_line.py listed eight block faces and this was not one of them — so there was no built line to adopt under T-0104 and the margin is the whole of the rule. THE ONE READING THE FACE ALREADY CARRIED AGREES WITH IT, and it is worth recording because nothing made it: temple_lake_st_building, a documented record that declares no frontage and was placed by another parcel entirely, stands with its front wall 1.492 m off this face at 75.73-82.52 m along. The run this parcel builds stands at 1.499 m, 7 mm outside it, and stops 3.90 m short of it along the face. So the Lake face of this block reads as one street line rather than two, which is the defect T-0104 exists to prevent, and it reads that way because the plat module's margin and a building nobody aligned to it happen to agree — not because this run adopted anything. Lot 4 is an interior lot and not a corner one, so the standard's third clause, that a corner lot builds to the corner, has nothing to bind here; the run stands off both of its own side lines by that same margin.
